clusters.name: Jonah's move to the conservatory, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around Jonah's arrival at Wexley Conservatory in September 1991, within months: his wrist injury stopped his playing in October, his anxiety and functioning fell; he and Rafe clashed and Rafe left their room; Jonah grew high and absorbed in radios; by January 1992 he was lost and low, unable to get going. His grandfather Gordon died in June 1991, before the move, and Jonah draws a near-total blank on family life across those years, so every shift that counts in these months is his own.

clusters.name: Grandfather Clifford's return to the family, 1989–1992
clusters.reason: Around Clifford coming back into the family in early 1989 after years away, within three years: the household moved twice, to Quarry Lane and then to the rebuilt Hollin Road, growing loud and cramped; Jonah's late nights rose in September 1989; he dropped chess and debate; his sister Tara was born in July 1990; in March 1991 his mother filled in his college forms and he underfunctioned, choosing his college by where his friend Rafe was headed. Shifts in anxiety, functioning and relationship moves pile up across these years around the moves and Tara's arrival, with Jonah's own trouble at their centre.

clusters.name: Grandmother Winifred's cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around Winifred's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002, over roughly two years: Jonah's performing fell away, his anxiety and functioning fell in September 2001; he had a disastrous audition in early 2002 and was done with performing; he grew distant from family and friends in September 2002; he left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol, moved to Fenwick to live with her, and when they split within the year he sank into deep depression in autumn 2003; back in Thornbury after the split, he could not face his family, his anxiety rose, and he relied on friends Silas, Corbin and Dale; Winifred died in February 2004. Jonah's distance from his parents held alongside his mother's burden of Winifred's care, and his functioning fell as hers was drawn to Winifred's sickroom.

clusters.name: Jonah's grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: in July 2008, while Jonah was at Alder Creek building with Silas before nursing school, he grew too drained for conversation with his mother; she pressed him to visit and he kept the door shut on her; the visit went wrong and she never got inside. In August 2008 he left for nursing school at Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to his mother; the silence held for roughly a year. His cutoff from his mother came within months of his grandmother's death and his own rest before nursing school began, when he was already braced for change.

clusters.name: Jonah's marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around Jonah's marriage to Wren in March 2017, over two and a half years: contact with his mother eased off slightly once he had Wren and her family; in October 2019 cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis; in the same month Jonah's contact with his mother shifted toward shorter, regular calls; later that month Wren was swamped with one thing after another—a street party, a fundraising dinner, the drive to the lake for her mother's retirement—and her anxiety and functioning fell; Jonah overfunctioned, laying out a plan to settle her; Wren's family talks all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear; once the weekend had a plan the dinner went well and Wren's anxiety fell and functioning rose; but at the lake weekend Jonah was awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, his symptom and anxiety up, his relationship to Wren distant; Wren grew anxious when he had had no sleep at family occasions. Shifts in Jonah's and Wren's functioning, anxiety and relationship moves pile up around the marriage and her family's closeness, with Wren's swamping drawing Jonah into overfunctioning and his own sleep failing around her family.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
